rationale: Chomp is a game-tree/search-heavy McGill benchmark with small integer-oriented functions, hot recursion, and no static function or line metadata available, so the table favors high-gain, low-risk passes and only moderately tolerates overhead: FLA and BCF get the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain since control-flow obscuring of game-tree search and move loops gives the strongest reverse-engineering resistance, with moderate RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so they apply where features indicate acceptable hot-loop cost; SUB and SPLIT are kept strongly favored because they are cheap, correctness-safe transforms that add instruction-level diversity at negligible runtime/size penalty; IBR and ICALL get mid-range security gains with higher CorrectnessRisk weights so indirect branching/call lowering is applied selectively on non-recursive, cold functions rather than chomp's recursive search path; IGV receives the lowest security value and highest CorrectnessRisk since global-variable indirection offers marginal benefit on a mostly local-variable game-logic program and risks breaking pointer/global interactions, making it apply only where diversity features strongly favor it.
